record.paper_title: Some open problems on well-filtered spaces and sober spaces
record.original_question: Let K be a full subcategory of Top0 containing Sob. If {X_i}_{i in I} is an arbitrary family of K-determined T0 spaces, is the product space prod_i X_i also K-determined?

evidence.quote: Question 5.22. ([49]) Let K be a full category of Top0 containing Sob (in particular, a Keimel-Lawson category). Is the product space of an arbitrary family of K-determined spaces K-determined?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbf{Top}_0$ denote the category of $T_0$ topological spaces with continuous maps, and let $\mathbf{Sob}$ denote its full subcategory of sober spaces. For a $T_0$ space $X$, write $X^s$ for its sobrification together with the canonical topological embedding $\eta_X : X \hookrightarrow X^s$.

Let $\mathbf{K}$ be a full subcategory of $\mathbf{Top}_0$ that contains $\mathbf{Sob}$. A $T_0$ space $Y$ is called a $\mathbf{K}$-space if $Y \in \mathrm{ob}(\mathbf{K})$. For an arbitrary $T_0$ space $X$, define the $\mathbf{K}$-completion $X^k$ to be the smallest subspace of $X^s$ that contains $\eta_X(X)$ and is itself a $\mathbf{K}$-space (assume $\mathbf{K}$ is such that this subspace is well-defined; for instance, $\mathbf{K}$ may be assumed to be a Keimel–Lawson category, i.e., closed under the formation of such completions and intersections of $\mathbf{K}$-subspaces inside any sober space). A $T_0$ space $X$ is called $\mathbf{K}$-determined if every continuous map $f : X \to Y$ into any $\mathbf{K}$-space $Y$ extends uniquely to a continuous map $\widehat{f} : X^k \to Y$ along $\eta_X^k : X \to X^k$.

Question: Given any family $\{X_i\}_{i \in I}$ of $\mathbf{K}$-determined $T_0$ spaces, is the Tychonoff product $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ also $\mathbf{K}$-determined?
artifact.status_search_result: Web search surfaces work on K-determined spaces and Keimel–Lawson categories (notably arXiv:1909.09303 and follow-up papers on well-filtered and sober spaces), but no source explicitly resolves whether products of K-determined T0 spaces are K-determined in general. The problem appears to still be listed as an open question in the literature on non-Hausdorff topology.

status_evidence.title: On T0 spaces determined by well-filtered spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Introduces K-determined spaces relative to a full subcategory K of Top0 containing Sob and discusses preservation properties.
status_evidence.claim: Source where the notion of K-determined space is developed; the product preservation question is posed as open.

status_evidence.title: Non-reflective categories of some kinds of weakly sober spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Related study of categories of weakly sober spaces; does not announce a resolution of the product question for K-determined spaces.
status_evidence.claim: No resolution of the product-of-K-determined-spaces question is provided.
